look_here_first: Start with the life cycle and leaves. Tetraneuris linearifolia is the annual Tetraneuris: slender stems with narrow linear to narrowly oblanceolate leaves, often hairy and gland-dotted. Then confirm the solitary yellow heads, hairy multi-series phyllaries, and the characteristic four-to-eight scale-like pappus structures.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaves alternate, simple, very narrow linear to narrowly oblanceolate/spatulate

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: solitary radiate yellow heads on long slender peduncles

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: involucre with multiple series of distinct phyllaries

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: ray florets yellow and typically 3-lobed at the tips

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: cypselae with a persistent pappus of several scale-like units

key_traits.label: Family training
key_traits.text: Use this species as an Asteraceae comparison where vegetative characters matter before the head is dissected: linear foliage and woolly/hairy texture are strong field cues, but final confirmation comes from capitulum, phyllaries, ray/disc florets and cypsela/pappus.

key_traits.label: Video training
key_traits.text: Use the Edwards Plateau frames for whole-plant habit and woolly linear foliage, then the Southern Texas frame for the underside of the capitulum and phyllary architecture.
